sentences.speaker: 片头片尾
sentences.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English.

sentences.speaker: 片头片尾
sentences.text: I'm Georgie and I'm Neil.

sentences.speaker: 片头片尾
sentences.text: You can find a video version of this podcast on our website at bbc learningenglish com, where you can find a free worksheet to download and subtitles to help you learn.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Hi, Neil.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: How are you?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I'm very well, thank you, Georgie.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Are you enjoying your coffee?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I am, but it's got a bit cool now.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I prefer my coffee hot, but oh well.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Are you enjoying yours?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I've finished mine.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Oh, that's a shame.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: It's a sad moment when I've finished my second coffee of the day because that's it.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I don't have more than two.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: So,

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Georgie, we're talking about coffee.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: How much coffee or how many coffees, if we're talking about cups of coffee, how many do you have a day?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I usually have two, and I know that you do as well, because we drink them both in the office, don't we?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: We have one cup of coffee in the morning and one usually in the afternoon when we need to regain some energy and alertness.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Yeah.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: And so we all know, because we make each other At BBC Learning English, we make each other coffee so we know how we take our coffee.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Yes.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: How we take our coffee is how we like it, what we like to put in it.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: For example, sugar or milk.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I know that you don't like milk in your coffee.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: You take your coffee black.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I do.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I like black coffee and you take your coffee white and you used to have sugar, but you don't anymore.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: That's right.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Occasionally, when I'm at home, I put some honey in my coffee to make it a bit sweeter.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Honey in coffee?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Yes.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Is that surprising?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I've never heard of that.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Really?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Sugar, but not honey.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: But why would that be so bad?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Well, I don't know.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: It's just I've never heard of it.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: It's really good.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I would recommend.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Okay.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: So, Georgie, what happens if you don't have your coffee?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Well, in the morning, if I don't have coffee, I feel very grumpy and very tired.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: In the afternoon, if I don't have a coffee, it's not terrible, but I would prefer to have my afternoon coffee.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: How about you?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Yeah, I need my coffee, especially in the morning, but I don't have my coffee first thing in the morning.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Oh, interesting.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I have it kind of, I don't know, work time, nine o'clock.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Why is that?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I think it's too strong, too powerful, Or maybe just the way I drink it.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Mmm.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: What happens if you drink too much coffee?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Oh,

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: then it's difficult to sleep because of the caffeine.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Caffeine is that chemical in coffee and tea that makes you feel awake and alert, But too much means you're too alert.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I don't think that caffeine has a big effect on me.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: I don't think I have trouble sleeping if I drink too much coffee.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: It's strange.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Yeah, because sometimes I'll have an espresso after dinner.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Really?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Yeah, And I can still sleep.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: That's crazy.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Yeah, Lucky me.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Lucky you.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Neil, have you ever tried to cut down on coffee?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Cut down on, You mean have less?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: No, I haven't tried to cut down on coffee, but I've tried to cut down on caffeine.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Okay.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: So I, for a while, I only drank decaffeinated coffee or decaf, as we call it.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Okay,

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: And how was that?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Well, I didn't miss caffeine at the time.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I don't think It lasted for a long time, um, but now I drink caffeine.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I don't care.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Okay,

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Neil, it's time to recap the vocabulary we used in the conversation.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: We used the verb take.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: So, Neil, how do you take your coffee?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I take my coffee black, and I know you take your coffee white.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Yes, We also heard caffeine, which is the chemical that is in coffee, which makes you feel more awake.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Yes, but you can also get decaffeinated coffee or tea.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Itmeans there's no caffeine And we usually shorten that just to decaf, decaf coffee.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Yes, We also heard the phrasal verb cut down on, which means you have less of something.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Yep, And you can also say cut back on.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: It means the same thing.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Okay,

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Well that is the end of this conversation about coffee in Real Easy English.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Yes, and if people want to watch more episodes of Real Easy English, what should they do?

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: They should go to our website, bbclearningenglish com, where they can find a free worksheet to test what they've learned.

sentences.speaker: Georgie
sentences.text: Goodbye for now.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Goodbye.
